questions.q: Question: A store window in which goods are displayed. Answer:
questions.n: This is the specific term used in the code to describe the glazed portion of a storefront used for displaying merchandise.

questions.q: Question: Minimum lateral spacing for plastic skylights. (sec 1604.2.c) Answer:
questions.n: According to Sec 1604, plastic skylights must be separated laterally by a minimum distance of 2.50 meters.

questions.q: Question: Minimum spacing for plastic skylights along the slope of the roof. (sec 1604.2.c) Answer:
questions.n: The code requires a larger buffer of 3.00 meters when measuring along the roof slope to account for heat and smoke travel.

questions.q: Question: Minimum distance of a sign from any electrical post or telephone wires. (sec 2004.1.d) Answer:
questions.n: For safety and maintenance access, signs must maintain a clear 1.00 meter distance from utility lines.

questions.q: Question: Maximum width of a business sign. Answer:
questions.n: The code restricts the maximum width of business signs to 1.20 meters to prevent excessive encroachment and visual clutter.

questions.q: Question: Minimum size of thread for an entrance or exit step. (sec 811.12.a.v.) Answer:
questions.n: The code specifies 300mm to ensure a full footing for safety during building ingress and egress.

questions.q: Question: Minimum number of steps for an entrance or exit step. (sec 811.12.a.v.) Answer:
questions.n: The provision requires at least two steps for these specific conditions to be clearly navigable.

questions.q: Question: Maximum slope for an entrance or exit ramp. (sec 811.12.a.iv) Answer:
questions.n: Sec 811.12.a.iv allows a maximum slope of 1:10 for these specific entrance/exit ramps.

questions.q: Question: Standard turn circle of a wheelchair. Answer:
questions.n: A 1.50-meter diameter is the standard space required to allow a wheelchair to complete a full turn.

questions.q: Question: Standard size of a perpendicular or diagonal parking slot. (sec 707.4.b.) Answer:
questions.n: Standard perpendicular parking requires a width of 2.50m and a length of 5.00m.

questions.q: Question: Standard size of a parallel parking slot. (sec 707.4.b.) Answer:
questions.n: For parallel parking, the width is reduced to 2.15 meters while maintaining the 5.00-meter length.

questions.q: Question: Hotel building parking ratio. (table VII.4.B) Answer:
questions.n: The NBC requires one parking slot for every three guest rooms in hotel buildings.

questions.q: Question: Public Hospital building parking ratio. (table VII.4.D) Answer:
questions.n: Public hospitals have a lower requirement of one slot per twenty-five beds.

questions.q: Question: Private Hospital building parking ratio. (table VII.4.D) Answer:
questions.n: Private hospitals require one slot for every twelve beds to accommodate more private vehicles.

questions.q: Question: Maximum distance of a handicapped parking from the facility being served. Answer:
questions.n: To ensure accessibility, handicapped parking must be located within 60 meters of the facility entrance.

questions.q: Question: Public Colleges and university parking ratio. (table VII.4.C) Answer:
questions.n: Public educational institutions require one parking slot per five classrooms.

questions.q: Question: Private Colleges and university parking ratio. (table VII.4.C) Answer:
questions.n: Private institutions have a stricter requirement of one slot per three classrooms.

questions.q: Question: Theaters, cinemas, auditoria, and stadia parking ratio. (table VII.4.E) Answer:
questions.n: The code mandates one slot for every 50 square meters of the area where spectators are located.

questions.q: Question: Chuches and othe places of worships parking ratio. (table VII.4.E) Answer:
questions.n: The requirement is one slot per 50 square meters of the area designated for the congregation.

questions.q: Question: Minimum rise & run of a stair for Group A dwellings (sec 708.8) Answer:
questions.n: For simple residential (Group A) dwellings, the code allows a minimum dimension of 200mm.

questions.q: Question: Minimum unobstructed headroom clearance from 3rd to succeeding floors. (sec 805.1) Answer:
questions.n: The code allows the ceiling height to drop to 2.10 meters for the third floor and above.

questions.q: Question: Minimum area of rooms for Human habitation. (sec 806.1.a) Answer:
questions.n: Any room intended for human habitation must have at least 6.00 square meters of floor area.

questions.q: Question: Least dimension of rooms for human habitation. (sec 806.1.a) Answer:
questions.n: The smallest side of a room for human habitation cannot be less than 2.00 meters.

questions.q: Question: Least dimension of an air duct. (sec 809.3) Answer:
questions.n: The code requires the smallest dimension of an air duct to be at least 300mm.

questions.q: Question: Max. encroachment into a public sidewalk of a foundation at least 600 mm below the grade. (sec 1002.3) Answer:
questions.n: Foundations may encroach up to 500mm into a sidewalk if they are deep enough (600mm below grade).

questions.q: Question: Max. encroachment into a public highway of a foundation at least 600 mm below the grade. (sec 1002.3) Answer:
questions.n: For public highways, the allowed encroachment is reduced to 300mm to protect main utility lines.

questions.q: Question: Minimum dimension of an exit door. (sec 1207.2.3.c) Answer:
questions.n: Exit doors must be at least 0.90 meters wide and 2.00 meters high.

questions.q: Question: Maximum width reduced by trim, handrails & fully-opened doors to corridors & exit balconies. (sec 1207.4) Answer:
questions.n: The code allows a total reduction of up to 200mm in the width of corridors and balconies by architectural features.

questions.q: Question: Minimum width of stairs serving more than 50 occupants. (sec 1207.5.a) Answer:
questions.n: When serving more than 50 people, the stair width must be at least 1.10 meters.

questions.q: Question: Minimum width of stairs serving less than 50 occupants. (sec 1207.5.a) Answer:
questions.n: For fewer than 50 occupants, the required width is reduced to 0.90 meters.

questions.q: Question: Minimum width of stairs serving less than 10 occupants. (sec 1207.5.a) Answer:
questions.n: In very small occupancy situations (under 10), the code permits stairs as narrow as 0.75 meters.

questions.q: Question: Maximum reduction in width of a stair due to trims and handrails. (sec 1207.5.a) Answer:
questions.n: Handrails and trim may not reduce the required width of a stair by more than 100mm.

questions.q: Question: Minimum run of a winding stair at any point of the steps. (sec 1207.5.) Answer:
questions.n: For winding stairs, the tread must be at least 150mm even at its narrowest point.

questions.q: Question: Allowable maximum vatriations tolerance in the rise and run of every step. (sec 1207.5.b) Answer:
questions.n: The variation between the largest and smallest riser or tread in a flight must not exceed 5mm.

questions.q: Question: Width of stair requiring an intermediate handrail. (sec 1207.5.h) Answer:
questions.n: When a stair is 3.00 meters wide or more, it must have an intermediate handrail to ensure safety.

questions.q: Question: Minimum width of an aisle serving both sides. (sec 1207.12.a) Answer:
questions.n: The code requires a minimum of 1.00 meter for aisles serving seats on both sides.

questions.q: Question: Minimum width of an aisle serving one side only. (sec 1207.12.a) Answer:
questions.n: Surprisingly, the code maintains the 1.00 meter minimum even if the aisle serves only one side.

questions.q: Question: Minimum distance between the back of each seat to the front of the seat behind it. (sec 1207.14.c.i) Answer:
questions.n: A minimum clear spacing of 300mm is required between seat rows for egress.

questions.q: Question: Maximum width of seat in a stand. (sec 1207.14.c.iii) Answer:
questions.n: In stands, the maximum seat width is specified as 480mm to control occupancy density.

questions.q: Question: Maximum projection of a penthouse or other projections above the roof. (sec 1210.1) Answer:
questions.n: Penthouses and other roof projections are limited to a maximum height of 8.40 meters above the roof.

questions.q: Question: Maximum ratio of a penthouse area to that of the supporting roof. (sec 1210.2) Answer:
questions.n: The area of the penthouse must not exceed one-third of the total area of the roof it sits on.

questions.q: Question: Minimum thickness of walls of masonry chimney for residentials. (sec 1211.1.b.i) Answer:
questions.n: Residential masonry chimney walls must be at least 100mm thick.

questions.q: Question: Minimum thickness of rubble stone masonry chimney for residentials. (sec 1211.1.b.i) Answer:
questions.n: Rubble stone masonry chimneys must be significantly thicker, at 300mm minimum.

questions.q: Question: Minimum number of storeys requiring one (1) or more dry standpipes. (sec 1212.2) Answer:
questions.n: Buildings with 4 or more storeys are required to have dry standpipes installed.

questions.q: Question: Minimum volume of water a dry standpipe should provide. (sec 1212.2.b) Answer:
questions.n: The system must be capable of delivering 900 liters per minute.

questions.q: Question: Diameter of a dry standpipe requiring a two-way Siamese connection. (sec 1212.2.e) Answer:
questions.n: A 4-inch (100mm) standpipe requires a two-way Siamese connection.

questions.q: Question: Diameter of a dry standpipe requiring a three-way Siamese connection. (sec 1212.2.e) Answer:
questions.n: A 5-inch (125mm) standpipe requires a three-way Siamese connection.

questions.q: Question: Diameter of a dry standpipe requiring a four-way Siamese connection. (sec 1212.2.e) Answer:
questions.n: A 6-inch (150mm) standpipe requires a four-way Siamese connection to handle the volume.

questions.q: Question: Minimum height of siamese connection on the street-front of the building. (sec 1212.2.e.) Answer:
questions.n: The connection must be at least 300mm above the grade.

questions.q: Question: Maximum height of siamese connection on the street-front of the building. (sec 1212.2.e.) Answer:
questions.n: The Siamese connection must not be placed higher than 1.2 meters above the grade.
